title.en: Discrete event ordering and replay determinism

summary: Verify that model time comes from the event queue, that ties break deterministically and that replays match.
objective: Two runs from the same initial state produce identical event logs, and playback speed changes only wall-clock duration.
applies_when: Entities move between queues, resources and destinations under a discrete-event model.
Several events can be scheduled for the same model time.
A viewer can change playback speed, pause or replay the scenario.
intent_signals: the sorter gives different results each run
check that speeding up playback does not change the outcome
example_prompts: Check that this parcel sorter replays identically at any playback speed.

principles: Model time belongs to the event queue; animation duration is a rendering artifact and must never advance or gate the model.
Simultaneity is normal, so the queue needs a total order: scheduled time first and then a declared tie-break such as a strictly increasing insertion counter, otherwise replays diverge.
Every state change is the effect of a dequeued event; a state change made inside a render callback is outside the model and cannot be replayed.
implementation: Log each scheduled and executed event as model time, tie-break key, event type and entity ID, and keep the log for the whole run.
Author a fixture that forces ties: two arrivals at the same time, a service completion coinciding with an arrival, and a cancellation scheduled at the same time as the event it cancels.
Run the fixture twice from the same initial state and compare logs line by line, then run it again at a different playback speed and with the window backgrounded.
Search the queue for any event scheduled earlier than the current model time; that is the signature of a callback writing state directly.
observable_checks: The two runs produce identical logs entry for entry, including the order of tied events.
Changing playback speed changes wall-clock duration only: model timestamps, ordering and final counts are unchanged.
No event is dequeued with a timestamp earlier than the previous one; a violation names the code path that bypassed the queue.

known_limits: Determinism of the trace says nothing about whether the authored arrival and service times resemble any real operation.
Authored verification guidance; no simulation was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: In this discrete-event framework the queue keys events by scheduled time with a strictly increasing event identifier as tie-break, so events scheduled for the same time are processed in the order they were scheduled.
claims.scope: SimPy scheduling documentation; other frameworks define their own tie-break, which must be declared rather than assumed.
